The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) indicated this in what is reported: that he and his companions ate dates and drank water upon them, and he said: "Praise be to Allah who fed us and gave us drink and made us Muslims."[[I have not found it in this form. There is confusion in it, perhaps from the copyist. It is derived from two hadiths: one, recorded by al-Nasa'i, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabari and Ibn Mardawayh, from Jabir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ate fresh dates and they drank water. He said: 'This is part of the bliss about which you will be asked.'" Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi in al-Shama'il, and al-Nasa'i narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished a meal he would say: 'Praise be to Allah who fed us and gave us drink and made us Muslims.'"]]

From the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Alhakumu al-takathur, Allah will not hold him accountable for the bliss He bestowed upon him in the abode of this world, and he will be given a reward as if he had recited a thousand verses."[[Recorded by al-Tha'labi, al-Wahidi and Ibn Mardawayh with their chains going back to Ubayy ibn Ka'b.]]
